about: A22 (Cheap, clean, reliable, fair, secure): nine hand-made plans for Prairie Town, each run hour by hour through all 8,760 hours of 2025 with lesson 13's planning model (13-capstone.json costs, EIA and NREL, dated; town_year.json shapes from EIA-930). 'm' holds each plan's measures, solved in advance with HiGHS 1.15.1 so the nine plans show at once, and checked against fresh solves. Plans, tariffs, priority weights and radar scales are illustrative choices, not recommendations. Prairie Town is fictional.

groups.note: Low-income homes: household income under $40,000 in 2020 (four RECS brackets: under $5,000 to $39,999). U.S. 2020: 42.81 of 123.53 million homes (34.7%) and 386 of 1,305 billion kWh of home electricity (29.6%). Prairie Town's homes are assumed to split the same way.

gradedNote: Illustrative: under the income-graduated tariff a low-income home pays half the fixed charge of other homes.

reserve.note: Reserve margin = capacity counted at the peak / the year's peak demand - 1. Gas and nuclear count at their full size; wind and solar at their average output per MW built in the year's 100 highest-demand hours; a battery at its MW, or at MWh / 4 when it holds less than four hours. A simple rule chosen for this lesson; grid operators use more detailed methods (lesson 6).

scales.note: Fixed scales chosen for this lesson: the rim of the radar is the 'best' end, the center the 'worst'; values beyond an end are drawn at that end. Scores (0 at the center, 1 at the rim) feed the weighted sums. A value beyond an end scores the same as that end, so the weighted sums weigh only the plans that are unbeaten as shown.
